reasons.figure1: Both papers open with a results plot rather than an overview diagram, but Paper A's three-panel Figure 1 (p5) states the central failure more directly (optimism, coverage and false superiority versus K) than Paper B's two-panel optimism curves (p5).
reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables (pp5-7) share a consistent, clean style with short captions; Paper B's coverage-width scatter and boundary-stress figures (pp6-7) are informative but its captions are long and caveat-heavy.
reasons.experiments: Paper A supports its claims with a full synthetic grid, a real replay over 24 configurations on 2,048 questions, a prospectively locked audit, an exactly matched call-budget comparison and a duplication ablation (pp4-7, App. C-F). Paper B has a solid synthetic grid and a multiplier boundary failure, but uses only 8 prompts on 600 questions, its matched-budget comparison is an exploratory appendix item (p13), and its audit is a non-blinded replay (p7).
reasons.page_use: Paper A fills about 7.5 of ICML's 8 body pages; Paper B fills about 8 of ICLR's 9 pages, and part of that is spent on cost logging and AI/ethics statements; both papers have thin reference lists (9 and 7 entries).
reasons.clean_text: Paper B's body contains a dataset hash (p4), an endpoint alias, a file path 'artifacts/reproduction_resources.json' and talk of agent compute (p8), whereas Paper A confines hashes and commits to the appendix (p10).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract and introduction (p1) build a clear argument toward three linked contributions; Paper B's introduction (pp1-2) is heavily hedged with scope disclaimers, which weakens the flow.

reasons.title: Paper B's title (page 1), 'What Survives Prompt Search?', is catchy and specific, while Paper A's three-part title (page 1) is longer and more jargon-heavy.
reasons.figure1: Both Figure 1s are result plots rather than overview diagrams; Paper B's three-panel K-sweep (page 5) conveys the central effect more directly than Paper A's optimism-vs-n curves (page 5).
reasons.figures_tables: Paper B's figures and tables (pages 5–7) are consistent and clean with MCSE-annotated tables; Paper A's figures (pages 5–7) are also clean, but its Appendix D (page 13) describes a table that only appears on the next page.
reasons.experiments: Paper B is richer: 24 real configurations, 2,048 questions, a K sweep, a locked prospective audit, matched call-budget comparisons and a duplication ablation (pages 4–7); Paper A uses only 8 prompts on 600 questions, and its real audit is a replay illustration (page 7).
reasons.page_use: Paper A's body fills about 8 ICLR pages with 7 references (page 9); Paper B's body uses about 7.5 of 8 ICML pages with 9 references (page 8), so both use the space reasonably well.
reasons.clean_text: Paper A's body contains a dataset commit hash (page 4), an API alias, and a file path 'artifacts/reproduction_resources.json' (page 8); Paper B keeps hashes and file names in its appendix (page 10).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper B's abstract and introduction (page 1) are well motivated and flow like an ICML paper; Paper A's abstract (page 1) is dense and hedged, and its introduction spends much space on scope disclaimers.

reasons.title: Paper A's question-plus-subtitle title (page 1) is somewhat long but vivid and specific; Paper B's title (page 1) is clear and descriptive but flatter, so the two are roughly equal.

reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables (pages 5–7) are consistent and compact, with clean booktabs tables; Paper B's figures are polished, but its long hedging captions (e.g., pages 7, 22, 25) read like disclaimers and its main tables are pushed to the appendix.
reasons.experiments: Paper A pairs a synthetic grid with a real 24-configuration, 49k-answer Qwen study that includes a locked audit, matched call budgets and a duplication ablation (pages 4–7); Paper B has a larger synthetic grid, but its real study shrank to 4 candidates after a runtime fallback (page 6), which weakens the real-model evidence.
reasons.page_use: Paper A fills about 7.5 ICML pages and adds a long appendix (pages 1–8); Paper B uses about 8 ICLR pages (pages 1–8), and both cite only 8–11 references, which is thin.

reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract and introduction (page 1) argue the problem and the three targets clearly; Paper B's abstract (page 1) is dense with numbers and caveats, and its introduction reads more hedged and procedural.

Auditing Scores, Gains, and Confidence After Benchmark Reuse' (p.1), is sharper and more memorable than Paper A's descriptive and somewhat generic 'Benchmark scores after prompt selection: accuracy, uncertainty, and reporting costs' (p.1); both are of acceptable length.

reasons.page_use: Paper A's body fills about 8 ICLR pages (pp.1–8) with 11 references, and Paper B fills about 7.5 of 8 ICML pages (pp.1–8) with 9 references, so both use the page limit adequately.

reasons.abstract_intro: Paper B's abstract and introduction (p.1) are well motivated and read like an ICML paper, whereas Paper A's abstract and body (pp.1–8) are dense with repeated caveats and hedging that obscure the main message.

reasons.title: Paper A's title (page 1) is long, with a question plus a three-line subtitle, while Paper B's title (page 1) is somewhat more specific and compact but still has a dense colon-and-list form; this is a minor edge for B.

reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables are consistent and clean, though many appendix pages hold a single small figure or table; Paper B's tables are clean but Figure 5 (page 8) is too small to read.
reasons.experiments: Paper B is much richer, with three models across two families, five worlds, five optimizer types, eight reporting protocols tested against known truth, a theory-based plug-in predictor and replications (pages 4-9, 15-16); Paper A's real-model evidence rests on one small model with four candidates and one partition (pages 6-8).
reasons.page_use: Paper A fills about 8 body pages of the ICLR format with 10 references (pages 1-8), while Paper B's body ends around page 7 of ICML's 8-page limit but cites more than 20 references.
reasons.clean_text: Paper A's body is mostly clean, but its appendix is full of script paths, a dataset hash and pipeline or role talk (pages 18-22); Paper B puts code/check_cond.py in the body (page 6) and script paths in the appendix (page 17).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper B's abstract is long but its introduction states the questions, approach and findings clearly in a NeurIPS/ICML style flow (pages 1-2); Paper A's abstract and text are dense with hedging qualifiers that make the argument hard to follow (pages 1-2).

reasons.title: Paper A's title (page 1) is long but specific and memorable, using the 'winner's curse' framing; Paper B's three-line question-style title (page 1) is longer and less crisp.
reasons.figure1: Both open with a results plot rather than a mechanism diagram: A's Figure 1 (page 5) shows the gap against n for three worlds and is clean and readable, while B's Figure 1 (page 5) is small and its legend is cramped.
reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables (pages 4-9) share one consistent style with compact clean tables, though Figure 5 on page 8 is tiny; Paper B's main-text figures (pages 5-9) are small and sparse, and most of its tables are pushed into the appendix interleaved with checklist pages (pages 13-21).
reasons.experiments: Paper A tests five real worlds with three models from two families, five optimizers, eight protocols, synthetic checks of its propositions and claim-distortion analyses (pages 4-8, 15); Paper B has a thorough synthetic grid but only one small real model with K=60 (page 8).
reasons.page_use: Paper A uses the ICML limit with about 7.5 body pages plus references (pages 1-8); Paper B fills 9 NeurIPS pages, but its appendix includes an empty Section C heading (page 13).
reasons.clean_text: Paper A cites a script path (code/check_cond.py) in the body on page 6 and has file paths and a hash in its appendix (pages 10, 17); Paper B's body is cleaner, though its appendix names analysis/*.py and REPRODUCE.md (pages 11, 13).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract is dense but structured and its introduction states Q1/Q2, findings and contributions clearly with solid related work (pages 1-2); Paper B's abstract is very long and number-heavy (page 1), though its introduction and related work are reasonable.

reasons.title: Both titles are long two-part titles; Paper B's 'Winner's Curse of Automatic Prompt and Pipeline Search' (p.1) names the mechanism more crisply than Paper A's question-plus-subtitle (p.1).
reasons.figure1: Neither paper opens with an overview diagram: Paper A's Figure 1 (p.5) is a synthetic gap-vs-K plot, and Paper B's Figure 1 (p.5) is a clean three-panel plot of real-LLM gap vs n per optimizer, which bears more directly on the claim.
reasons.figures_tables: Paper A's figures and tables are consistent and readable (pp.5-9, 13-20); Paper B's are mostly clean, but Figure 5 (p.8) is tiny and hard to read, and its appendix tables are long dumps (p.14).
reasons.experiments: Paper B combines propositions with proofs (p.3), five real worlds across three models and two families, five optimizer types, eight protocols, and pool-bootstrap and without-replacement checks (pp.4-16); Paper A is thorough on synthetic cells but has only one small real model over 60 configurations (p.8).
reasons.page_use: Paper A fills about 9 NeurIPS pages with roughly 15 references (pp.1-9); Paper B's body ends on p.7 of an 8-page ICML limit, which is slightly short, but it has about 24 references.
reasons.clean_text: Both leak artifacts: Paper A puts a data revision hash in the body (p.4) and file names in the appendix (p.11, 13); Paper B cites 'code/check_cond.py' in the body (p.6), and its appendix carries script maps and agent narrative (p.17).
reasons.abstract_intro: Paper A's abstract (p.1) is very long and number-dense; Paper B's abstract is also dense, but its introduction states the questions, approach, findings and contributions in a standard ICML flow (pp.1-2).
